key_insight: GPU-optimized fast diagonalization and matrix-free preconditioning accelerate high-order finite-element elliptic solves by reducing both iteration counts and per-iteration cost.
engineering_relevance: Faster distributed elliptic solvers can reduce computational bottlenecks in engineering simulations using high-order finite elements.
method: Distributed direct fast diagonalization for tensor-product meshes with direction-wise grading and coefficients varying along one coordinate.
Hybrid Schwarz with exact FD cell inverses and Chebyshev–Jacobi p-multigrid, both supporting hanging-node octrees.
CUDA, HIP and SYCL implementations with selective FP32 computation, FP64 conjugate gradients and adaptive coarse-level distribution.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 100–1,000× faster direct solves than Jacobi PCG on uniform meshes and 11 HS-FD iterations on octrees across 8–1,024 MI250X graphics compute dies.
watch_item: Direct fast diagonalization requires suitable tensor-product structure and restricted coefficient variation; solver and precision choices depend on mesh and operator properties.
paper_title: Accelerating matrix-free fast diagonalization and preconditioned linear solvers for high-order finite element discretized elliptic problems on distributed GPUs
